messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the firewall rollout we just pushed, KMS egress from prod GPU nodes is failing. GPU onboarding is stuck, warm pool counts dropping. :warning:

sam: Saw the scaling alarms earlier. Any logs we can share?

maria: Node bootstrap shows repeated `KMS::ConnectTimeout` then `keystore proxy 503`. NATGW conntrack is spiking. Snippet:
```
2026-03-20T10:12:03Z ERROR k8s/bootstrap: connect to kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com:443: connection refused
keystore: proxy returned 503
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: firewall-default-deny v2 -> prod at 2026-03-20T10:09Z (rolled by @ops-lead)

vikram: Is that the new deny that blocks outbound 443 to the KMS IP ranges? Looks like the rule was a broad deny for privatelink exceptions.

jordan: We do have an EU fallback keystore but routing policy pins nodes to regional keystores; us-east nodes can't hit eu fallback automatically.

sam: Immediate mitigation options: allow egress from gpu-subnet to `kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com` or add a privatelink route. If we open egress via NATGW we'll see burst NAT costs — rough estimate $1.2k/day if sustained.

security-oncall: From compliance POV prefer an explicit, timeboxed firewall exception rather than global open 443. Need change logged + audit labels so we can trace.

maria: Proposed plan: 1) temporary firewall exception for the service account CIDR -> kms.us-east-1 FQDN 2) route to privatelink where available 3) annotate change with audit tags and TTL 4) follow-up postmortem. Creating ticket ENGINFRA-903.

vikram: If we open an exception, add an audit annotation like `fw:temp_kms_exception` and TTL=4h. Also run `tcpdump` on the NAT to confirm TLS handshake resumes.

jordan: I'll patch the egress security group and add tag `ticket:ENGINFRA-903` now. ETA ~7m. Patch will look like:
```bash
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0gpu --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.24.0.0/18 --description "temp kms exception ENGINFRA-903"
```

ops-bot: change-request ENGINFRA-903 submitted -> approved by ops-lead. Applying patch.

sam: After patch, add a canary for node onboarding to validate warm pool recovery. Also need a follow-up to audit the default-deny rules and map privatelink coverage: ENGINFRA-904.

security-oncall: I'll export the last 24h of audit logs to the compliance bucket and mark retention for this incident. Tagging for SOC review.

maria: Patch applied, warm pools are climbing back to target. Running a live onboarding canary now. If stable we'll close ENGINFRA-903 and run the postmortem with follow-ups (ENGINFRA-904 + SOC review). Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
